\caption{Ruleset-size scalability (input fixed), per folding step, on \textsc{ClamAV} (left) and \textsc{MS-DLP} (right). \emph{Top:} absolute circuit size with the single-rule framework floor (dotted; $8.19$\,M R1CS for \textsc{ClamAV}, $0.08$\,M for \textsc{MS-DLP}); growing the ruleset to the full $38{,}875$ (\textsc{ClamAV}) / $9{,}861$ (\textsc{MS-DLP}) rules grows the circuit far slower than the rule count. \emph{Bottom:} net circuit cost \emph{per rule per input byte}---cumulative R1CS above the floor divided by cumulative rule count times per-step input length---moving from $0.45\times10^{-3}$ to $0.76\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{gdb}) and $0.25\times10^{-3}$ to $0.44\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{readelf}) R1CS per rule-byte (\textsc{ClamAV}) and $1448.30\times10^{-3}$ to $538.78\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{email1}) and $14.82\times10^{-3}$ to $1.53\times10^{-3}$ (\ttt{email2}) R1CS per rule-byte (\textsc{MS-DLP}) between $10\%$ of the ruleset and the full set. For the same \textsc{MS-DLP} ruleset, \textsc{Zombie} emits $77{,}463{,}552$ R1CS in total; dividing by the $2000$-byte input and the same $9{,}861$ rules gives $\sim$$3.93$ R1CS per rule-byte, the same normalization applied to BORA.}
